name: Semaglutide

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Rodent studies, incl. thyroid C-cell tumors

what.text: Semaglutide is a man-made version of GLP-1, a hormone the gut releases after eating. The Wegovy label says it shares 94% of its sequence with human GLP-1 and works by switching on the GLP-1 receptor. GLP-1 helps control appetite and how much food people eat.

src.label: Wegovy injection and tablets label, DailyMed

what.text: In animal studies, semaglutide reached and switched on nerve cells in brain areas that control food intake. That finding comes from animals. The label says the exact way it lowers heart risk in adults has not been established.

src.label: Wegovy injection and tablets label, DailyMed

what.text: The FDA-approved brands are Ozempic and Wegovy, given by injection under the skin, and Rybelsus, Ozempic tablets and Wegovy tablets, taken by mouth. All are made by Novo Nordisk.

research.text: Semaglutide has been tested in large randomized trials paid for by its maker, Novo Nordisk. Three are listed below exactly as they were run: a heart-safety trial in type 2 diabetes, the first large weight trial, and a heart-outcome trial in people without diabetes.

research.title: SUSTAIN-6: heart safety in type 2 diabetes

facts.v: randomized, placebo-controlled. Built to show semaglutide did not raise heart risk (a noninferiority test).
3,297 adults with type 2 diabetes on standard care. 83% had heart disease, chronic kidney disease, or both.
a weekly semaglutide injection (0.5 mg or 1.0 mg) or placebo
first heart-related death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke, counted together

research.found: The combined outcome happened in 6.6% of the semaglutide group and 8.9% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.74), which met the trial's safety goal. Eye complications of diabetic retinopathy were more common on semaglutide (hazard ratio 1.76). More people stopped semaglutide because of side effects, mainly stomach and bowel effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01720446.

src.label: Marso et al., SUSTAIN-6, N Engl J Med 2016

research.title: STEP 1: weight in adults without diabetes

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled. Two people got semaglutide for every one on placebo.
1,961 adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with at least one weight-related condition. None had diabetes.
a weekly 2.4 mg semaglutide injection or placebo, both with a lifestyle program
percent change in body weight, and how many people lost at least 5%

research.found: Average body weight changed by -14.9% on semaglutide and -2.4% on placebo. 86.4% on semaglutide and 31.5% on placebo lost at least 5%. Nausea and diarrhea were the most common side effects. 4.5% on semaglutide and 0.8% on placebo stopped treatment because of stomach and bowel effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03548935.

src.label: Wilding et al., STEP 1, N Engl J Med 2021
STEP 1 registry record, ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03548935)

research.title: SELECT: heart outcomes in people with obesity and heart disease

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, run until a set number of heart events had happened
17,604 adults aged 45 or older with existing heart or blood-vessel disease and a BMI of 27 or more. None had diabetes.
a weekly 2.4 mg semaglutide injection or placebo
heart-related death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke, counted together

research.found: The combined outcome happened in 6.5% of the semaglutide group and 8.0% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.80). 16.6% on semaglutide and 8.2% on placebo stopped the study drug for good because of side effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03574597.

src.label: Lincoff et al., SELECT, N Engl J Med 2023

research.text: The labels describe further trials behind the later approved uses: kidney outcomes in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease (Ozempic) and liver disease called MASH (Wegovy). Those trials are summarized in each label's Clinical Studies section.

research.text: In two-year studies, mice and rats given semaglutide under the skin developed more thyroid C-cell tumors, at exposures similar to those in people. It is not known whether this applies to humans. Semaglutide did not damage DNA in standard lab tests.

us.text: Semaglutide is FDA approved under three brand names: Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy. Compounded semaglutide is not FDA approved. FDA says the semaglutide shortage ended in February 2025. As of October 31, 2026.
Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

items.text: approved to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes, alongside diet and exercise. Also approved to lower the risk of major heart events in adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease, and to lower the risk of kidney decline, kidney failure and heart-related death in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.

items.text: semaglutide injections were on FDA's shortage list from 2022. On February 21, 2025, FDA said the shortage was resolved. Grace periods for compounders followed. For state-licensed pharmacies (section 503A) it ended after a court denied an injunction on April 24, 2025. For outsourcing facilities (section 503B) it ran until May 22, 2025.

src.label: FDA: Clarifies policies for compounders as GLP-1 supply stabilizes

items.text: on April 1, 2026, FDA said semaglutide is not on its drug shortage list and not on the 503B bulks list.

src.label: FDA: Clarifies policies for compounders as GLP-1 supply stabilizes

items.text: pharmacies may not regularly compound drugs that are essentially copies of a commercially available drug. FDA said it may consider a semaglutide injection combined with vitamin B12 to be essentially a copy when both amounts are within 10% of the strengths of available products, unless a prescriber documents a significant difference for an individual patient. FDA said it does not intend to act when a pharmacy fills four or fewer such prescriptions in a calendar month.

src.label: FDA: Clarifies policies for compounders as GLP-1 supply stabilizes

items.text: FDA says semaglutide sodium and semaglutide acetate are different active ingredients from the one in the approved drugs, and it knows of no lawful basis for compounding with them.

src.label: FDA: Concerns with unapproved GLP-1 drugs used for weight loss

items.text: on March 3, 2026, FDA announced 30 warning letters to telehealth companies over false or misleading claims about compounded GLP-1s, including claims that they are the same as approved drugs. A June 8, 2026 letter cited a site that called compounded semaglutide with B12 "the FDA approved active ingredient" combined with a vitamin and called its pharmacies "FDA approved". FDA said compounded drugs are not FDA approved and that pharmacies have no FDA-approved designation.

items.text: as of May 31, 2026, FDA had received 990 adverse event reports tied to compounded semaglutide. FDA says these are likely underreported, because most pharmacies do not have to report them. FDA has also received reports, some needing hospital care, linked to dosing errors with compounded semaglutide.

after.title: Sport
after.text: USADA says GLP-1 medicines, including semaglutide, are not prohibited in sport and need no therapeutic use exemption. USADA says semaglutide and tirzepatide are in WADA's 2027 Monitoring Program, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Monitored substances are not prohibited; labs test for them so WADA can study their use. We could not open WADA's own list to confirm.

side.text: Every semaglutide label has a boxed warning, FDA's strongest kind, about thyroid C-cell tumors. The most common side effects are stomach and bowel effects. The labels list other serious risks, below.

items.text: in mice and rats, semaglutide caused thyroid C-cell tumors. It is not known if it causes these tumors, including medullary thyroid cancer, in people. People with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer, or with MEN 2 syndrome, must not use it. Warning signs include a lump in the neck, trouble swallowing, shortness of breath and lasting hoarseness.

unconfirmed: Drugs@FDA's own web pages blocked automated access, so first-approval years come from FDA's Drugs@FDA dataset served through openFDA.
Australia's TGA website could not be reached, so semaglutide's status there (ARTG listing and the rules on compounding) is not shown.
WADA's website blocked access, so the 2026 and 2027 Prohibited Lists could not be opened; the sport status is taken from USADA.
The approved uses of Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy in Canada were not checked; only their listing in the Drug Product Database was.
The years each later US use (heart, kidney, MASH, children) was added were not confirmed from FDA approval letters, so they are not given.
surprises: FDA said in April 2026 that a semaglutide injection combined with vitamin B12 may count as essentially a copy of an approved drug, though adding B12 is often presented as making a compounded product different.
Compounding is often explained by the shortage, but FDA declared the semaglutide shortage resolved on February 21, 2025, and says semaglutide is not on its shortage list.
Some sellers call compounding pharmacies "FDA approved"; FDA says no such designation exists for pharmacies or outsourcing facilities.
The Wegovy label removed its warning section on suicidal behavior and ideation in February 2026.
Ozempic is widely used for weight loss, but its US label covers type 2 diabetes, heart and kidney uses only; the weight-management brand is Wegovy.
